title: Evolution experiment record
description: One attempt at the change a batch's analysis called for: its identity, the batch base it starts from, its durable ref, its append-only rounds, and the terminal decision that turns it into history (contract: Change lineage). This record — not `.ai-tasks/`, not a branch, not the checkout — is what makes an experiment discoverable, which is why it names its own task selections and candidate revisions rather than pointing at files that are machine-local or archived away.

experiment_id.description: `<batch-id>-exp-<NN>`, one past the highest ordinal its batch has ever used. Never reused: a historical experiment's name has to keep naming the attempt it was.

base_revision.description: The exact source commit this experiment starts from, frozen by the batch's first experiment. Every experiment of one batch carries the same value; a differing one is refused rather than reconciled (contract invariant 15).

base_release_ref.description: The most recent release tag reachable from `base_revision` at creation time, or null when the checkout had none. Recorded rather than re-derived so the record still states which released protocol this candidate builds on after the tag is gone (contract invariant 4 keeps missing fields explicit).

ref.description: The durable Git ref holding this experiment's rounds. Fast-forward only, so every pinned candidate revision stays reachable after the working branch is deleted.

rounds.description: Append-only. Exactly one round is open while the experiment is; a terminal experiment has all of them closed.

round.description: One revision pass: the tasks admitted into it and the candidate revision it produced. Replay evidence names a round, so closing one and opening the next is what makes prior evidence stale by construction.

reason.description: Why this round exists — the grouped admission for round 1, the revision reason afterwards.

candidate_revision.description: The ref tip observed when this round closed; null while the round is open, and immutable once pinned. Distinct from the promotion revision a promoted candidate later produces on the source line.

admitted_task.description: One draft's admission: which proposal it was, the bytes admitted, and the task the copy took. The hash is the provenance a copied draft would otherwise lose the moment either file is edited.

draft_id.description: The draft's stem under `batches/<batch-id>/proposed-tasks/`. A kebab slug, so it is one path segment with no traversal, no dot-file, and no extension to confuse for one. A draft may be consumed once; re-proposing the idea means a new id.

decision.description: The terminal decision, or null while the experiment is open. `superseded_by` is set only for `superseded` and `promotion_revision` only for `promoted`; both are present and null otherwise. The controller enforces that pairing, which the implemented JSON Schema subset cannot express — the fields stay explicit rather than optional so a record never leaves the reader guessing whether a value is absent or unrecorded.

superseded_by.description: The experiment that replaced this one. It belongs to the same batch and starts from the same base.

promotion_revision.description: The source-line commit carrying this candidate's change. Never the candidate tip it came from.
